newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares rebound with help from Danisco.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares rebound with help from Danisco.

text.p: Danish share prices turned upward on Friday, with a 1.5 percent gain by Danisco a major contributor to the 0.18 percent rise in the KFX top 20 shares index.
At 0745 GMT the KFX was up 0.31 point, to 171.54. Its August future was untraded at 172.50.

Danisco had been punished over the past two days for a forecast of 1997/98 profit growth less than 1996/97's 14 percent. It fell from 432.00 crowns before Wednesday's announcement, to 400.00 at Thursday's close, but on Friday morning was up to 406.00.

Tele Danmark was up one crown, to 345.00. On Wednesday the government said it intended to sell all or part of its 52 percent holding. On Thursday the company said it expected the selloff in 1998 and was considering buying some of the state's shares itself.
Novo Nordisk rose four crowns, to 727.00, despite some analysts' fears that its vital insulin sales could be threatened by a new generation of oral diabetic treatments.
Britain's New Scientist magazine on Thursday reported that Novo had developed a new enzyme that bleaches out colour running from one item to the rest of the wash.
